transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um, I guess I'm here because... well, it's probably not a huge deal, but I've been having a little trouble at work lately. I'm in advertising sales, and we have these really long strategy meetings. And I just... I keep getting up during them. 

Like, I know I'm supposed to stay seated with everyone else, but I always find an excuse to pop up, even if it's just to refill my water or, you know, pace over by the printer for a second. It's probably just a silly habit, but I just can't seem to stay in my chair when I'm supposed to, and it's starting to make me a little self-conscious. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
Do you often find yourself feeling worried or anxious about a wide range of different things, like your job performance, health, or personal finances, even when there isn't a specific reason to be?

Oh, um... no, I don't really think so. I mean, sales can be a little stressful sometimes, but just the normal amount, you know? I definitely don't sit around worrying about my health or finances if there's no reason to. I'm actually a pretty positive person overall! 

I hope that's okay to say, I just... I want to make sure I'm answering your questions right. Is that what you meant?
Looking back at your childhood and school years, were you frequently in trouble for breaking rules or acting without thinking about the consequences?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I was a pretty good kid, I think. I definitely wasn't, like, a troublemaker or anything like that. 

I guess sometimes I could be a little... energetic? Like maybe talking out of turn once in a while or just getting caught up in the moment playing with friends. But I always tried really hard to follow the rules and make my teachers happy. I definitely wasn't getting into serious trouble or doing bad things on purpose. 

I hope that answers your question? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
When you are working on tasks that aren't particularly exciting, do you often find it difficult to keep your mind on what you are doing without getting distracted?

Um, yeah, I guess I do have a little trouble with that sometimes. It's really not terrible, but... well, like, if I'm in one of those longer strategy meetings, or if I have to read through a really long client brief, I always start out super focused. I really want to do a good job! But then... I don't know, after a few minutes, I'll kind of realize that I've just been staring at the exact same slide, or the same paragraph, and I honestly have no idea what the last point even was. 

It's probably just normal fatigue, right? Like, everyone gets a little bored reading long documents? I always try to catch myself and refocus right away so I don't miss anything important. Does that sound like what you're asking about?
Looking back at your time in elementary school, did you often find it difficult to stay focused on your schoolwork or finish your assignments because your mind would wander?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I was a happy kid and I really loved school, but... yeah, I suppose my mind did wander sometimes. 

I actually remember, um, even way back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was really bright. But they also said I tended to rush through things, or I'd forget to turn in my homework. And my desk was always just... well, it was always stuffed with all these half-finished papers and things. I think I just got really excited about starting new projects and would forget to finish the old ones? And I guess I did talk out of turn sometimes, just because I was so eager to participate. 

It wasn't because I didn't care or anything, I just... I had a lot of energy, I think. Is that normal for kids that age? I hope that's the kind of example you were looking for.
Beyond getting up during meetings, do you find that you often feel restless, or feel a need to keep moving even when you're trying to relax?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely don't feel like I'm constantly pacing around or anything like that. When I'm home and it's time to relax, I really try to just unwind, you know? 

I guess maybe sometimes I might tap my foot a little bit, or... or fiddle with a pen if I'm watching TV, but I think that's just because I like keeping my hands busy. It's definitely not like a strong urge to run a marathon or anything. I'm pretty good at just sitting on the couch when I need to. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I am at home.
When you think about your daily life, do you feel that your struggles with focus and attention cause you more difficulty than your tendency to be restless or act on impulse?

Um, gosh, I'm not really sure how to answer that? I guess I haven't really thought about one being worse than the other, because... well, honestly, neither of them really causes me any *major* difficulties. 

I mean, I do pretty well at my job and everything! So I guess I haven't really noticed one standing out as a bigger problem than the other. Like, sometimes I get a little distracted with those long briefs, and sometimes I get a little eager and jump into a conversation, but they both just kind of... pop up now and then. I always try to handle it right away so it doesn't affect my work or my team. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just wouldn't want to exaggerate and say one is this huge struggle when I'm mostly doing fine. Does that make sense?
If you had to choose which is more frequent in your day-to-day life, would you say you struggle more with keeping your mind on tasks or with feeling the need to move and act impulsively?

Um, well... I guess if I absolutely had to pick one, maybe... maybe the focus thing happens a tiny bit more often? But honestly, they're both pretty mild. 

Like I said, I really try hard to stay on top of things. I might lose my train of thought for a second while I'm working on a client pitch, or maybe I'll talk a little fast if I'm excited about a new ad campaign, but... it's never anything I can't handle, you know? I just sort of course-correct and keep going. I definitely wouldn't say I'm constantly struggling with either one of them. 

I really hope I'm answering this right for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need without making it sound worse than it actually is. Is that helpful?
Have these patterns of being easily distracted or feeling the need to move been present consistently for at least the past six months?

Um, well, yes, I suppose it's been going on for a little while now. Definitely more than six months. I'd say I really started noticing these little things... oh, maybe around two years and two months ago? That was when I transitioned into advertising sales strategy. 

It was a big step up, and a lot more responsibility, so I think maybe I just had to adjust to the new workflow, you know? It's not that I've been struggling terribly the whole time, just that the little moments of losing focus or getting a bit fidgety started popping up around then. I've been managing it okay, though! I really try to stay organized so it doesn't become a problem for anyone else. 

I hope it's okay that it's been going on for that long? I probably should have mentioned it sooner, I just didn't want to make a big fuss if it was just normal stress from a new role. Does that make sense?
Looking back at your childhood before you were 12 years old, did you experience these same challenges with focusing or feeling the need to move around?

Um, gosh, well... if I really think back to when I was little, like before high school... I guess some of those things were there, too? 

I mean, I was always a good student! My elementary school teachers always said I was really bright. But, um, they did sometimes write on my report cards that I... well, that I rushed through things a bit, or maybe talked out of turn sometimes. And, um, I guess I did forget my homework every now and then. My desk was always a little... messy, I suppose. Just stuffed with papers I hadn't quite finished yet. 

But I promise I wasn't a bad kid or anything! I always wanted to do well and please my teachers. I just had a lot of energy and sometimes got a little ahead of myself. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a troublemaker? I really tried my best to be good. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?

You mentioned that you've been managing these things okay, but have these patterns ever caused you to make significant mistakes, miss important deadlines, or receive formal feedback from your supervisors about your performance?

Oh, um... well... I guess I wouldn't say *significant* mistakes... but, um, it has come up a little bit at work recently. I really, really try to keep everything perfect, but... well, my last performance review did mention a few little things. Just about, you know, attention to detail and following through on some of the smaller tasks. 

And, um... there was this one thing with a client recently. I guess I missed a few details in a pitch because I got a little sidetracked, and they did complain to my manager. It was just a miscommunication, really! But it made me feel awful, because I care *so* much about doing a good job and I would hate to damage any accounts or lose their trust. I've been trying extra hard since then to double-check everything. 

I really hope my boss doesn't think I'm a bad employee. I put in a lot of extra hours to make up for it! Does that sound like a normal thing to happen when you're busy, or is that the kind of mistake you're asking about?
Aside from your work environment, do you notice these same patterns of getting distracted or feeling the need to move around when you are at home or in other social settings?

Um, gosh, at home or with friends? I... I don't really think so. Or at least, I haven't really noticed it being an issue. 

I mean, I really try to be present when I'm with people. I'd absolutely hate for my friends or family to think I wasn't listening to them, you know? So I make a really big effort to be a good friend and focus on whatever we're doing. Maybe I get up to tidy the apartment a bit when I'm home, or I might shift around a tiny bit during a really long movie, but... that's just normal relaxing, right? It's definitely not like I'm bouncing around or ignoring anyone. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I struggle with those patterns in social settings or at home. I hope that's alright? Is it normal for these things to mostly just happen when you're under a lot of pressure at work?

When you are engaged in a hobby or a personal activity that you find relaxing, like reading a book or watching a movie, do you find yourself frequently unable to finish it because your mind wanders or you feel the need to do something else?

Um, well... with hobbies, like a fun book or a movie, I think I usually do okay! If it's something I really enjoy, I definitely want to see how it ends. 

But... I guess where I *do* notice that happening—the mind wandering part—is more with work things? Like, um, if I'm reading a long client brief or sitting in one of our longer strategy meetings. I always start out really focused, I promise I do! I have my notebook out and I'm ready to go. But then, after a few minutes, I'll suddenly realize I've just been staring at the exact same slide, or the same paragraph, and I have absolutely no idea what the last point was. 

I always feel so bad when it happens, but I try to just catch myself and reread it really quickly so I don't fall behind or let anyone down. I mean, those corporate documents can be pretty dense and dry, right? So it's probably pretty normal to zone out a little bit compared to when you're watching a fun movie... isn't it?

When you were a child, did your parents or family members ever mention that you had trouble focusing on tasks or staying still while at home, or was it mostly just something your teachers noticed at school?

Um... gosh, thinking back to when I was little... I think it was mostly at school? My parents didn't really say much about it at home. I mean, I was just a happy, energetic kid, you know? 

But, um... I do remember my teachers bringing it up, even way back in elementary school. It definitely started before high school. They were always really nice about it! They would tell my parents that I was bright and had a lot of potential... but they did mention, um, that I rushed through things sometimes. And that I maybe talked out of turn a little bit. 

I was just so eager to participate, I think! But I guess I did forget my homework sometimes, too. Oh, and my desk... it was always a bit of a mess, just stuffed with half-finished papers and drawings. I always meant to finish them, I really did! I just got excited about the next thing, I suppose. 

Does that sound like the kind of thing you're looking for? I hope I wasn't a bad kid or anything... I think a lot of kids are a little disorganized at that age, right?
When you are at home, do you ever find that you have difficulty organizing your personal activities or finishing chores, in a way that feels similar to the challenges you face with your work tasks?

Um, at home? Well, honestly, I think I'm okay with chores! I mean, I like having a tidy space, so I try really hard to keep things nice. 

But... I guess where I do struggle with organizing things—like you mentioned with work—is, well, work itself. Um, when I'm trying to pull together a campaign, I... I kind of end up with my notes everywhere. Like, some will be in my emails, some on sticky notes, some in my planner... and then I'll have all these random tabs open on my computer. 

I really do try to stay on top of it, but sometimes I end up wasting so much time just trying to figure out what I'm supposed to do first, instead of actually starting the work. I know that probably sounds a bit messy, and I'm really working on finding a better system! I'm sure everyone gets a little overwhelmed when they have a lot of different pieces to manage, right? Is it okay that I brought it back to work instead of home? I just wanted to be honest about where I actually notice it happening.

Looking at your overall behavior, would you say that your difficulties with staying still and acting without thinking are just as frequent and problematic as your difficulties with focus and organization, or are the focus issues definitely the main problem?

Um... gosh, that's a good question. I think... well, I really feel like the focus and organizing part is the main thing I struggle with. Like the stuff I was saying about my notes and the long meetings. 

As for the other part... staying still and acting without thinking... I don't really think I have a big problem with that? I mean, I try to be very polite and professional, especially at work! I definitely don't want to be disruptive or anything like that. I might, um, maybe I tap my foot a little bit if I've been sitting for a really long time, or maybe I get a little too excited and jump into a conversation too quickly sometimes... but I don't think it's a huge issue. 

I'm pretty good at catching myself and apologizing if I interrupt someone. I always want to make sure everyone feels heard! So, um, yeah, I'd say it's definitely more about the focus stuff for me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering these questions the right way for you...
